correctness.rationale: The original 27-vertex graph is specified by ternary coordinates and exact adjacency. The 1,404 nonempty faces and face vector (27,243,540,405,162,27) are reconstructed from 27 open neighborhoods. An explicit vertex-toggle matching pairs 672 faces and leaves critical vector (1,3,56,0,0,0). The complete directed Hasse diagram has 4,698 incidences, and a topological sort visits all 1,404 vertices, proving acyclicity; separate exact mod-two ranks (26,214,270,135,27) give matching Betti vector, so the matching is perfect. The 26 matched vertex-edge pairs form a tree, and exact elimination of 214 edge-triangle generators reduces the 540 triangle relations to three generators with exponent-balanced relators including witnesses for all three commutators. Hence \(\pi_1\cong\mathbb Z^3\). The two-dimensional Morse CW chain ranks and this pi1 give integral \(H_1\cong\mathbb Z^3\) and \(H_2\cong\mathbb Z^{56}\) with no higher groups; no integral torsion is inferred from mod-two ranks alone. All critical checks were replayed using the self-contained code from this package.

evidence: Kahle, arXiv:math/0512077, Lemma 2.3 proves an at-most-two-dimensional deformation retract for every \(K_{2,3}\)-free graph; H(3,3) meets that condition.
Matsushita, arXiv:1210.2803, and Behal–Chih, arXiv:2308.02938, provide overlapping general graph-walk pi1 results.
Shukla, arXiv:1802.04526, concerns maximum degree <=3 and certain 4-regular circulants, whereas H(3,3) has degree 6.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The abstract dimension bound and free-abelian pi1, together with elementary Euler counting, can account for the homology consequences; they are not novel in isolation. A general deformation retract does not imply that the original triangulation has a perfect acyclic face matching with each critical cell count exactly equal to the corresponding Betti number. No inspected broader theorem provides that stronger property, and its proof is supplied explicitly.

originality.rationale: The accepted assertion is the 672-pair perfect discrete-Morse matching on the 1,404-face original triangulation, with exact critical vector (1,3,56,0,0,0). It is not a bare claim of group, integral homology, or abstract two-dimensional homotopy dimension, which are covered or strongly implied by Matsushita, Behal–Chih and Kahle with elementary counting. After comparing actual scope and consequences, no inspected paper or indexed exact calculation yielded the stronger perfect original-triangulation face matching; an unindexed equivalent remains possible.
residual_risks: Another indexed or unindexed source may give a special perfect acyclic matching under a different construction name.

General two-dimensional deformation, Hamming graph-walk group calculations, and easy Euler-characteristic arithmetic substantially reduce novelty of the homology consequences; those are not the acceptance basis.
The construction gives optimal Morse cell counts but not canonical two-cell attaching maps or a full homotopy decomposition.

value.rationale: An optimal discrete-Morse vector on the *original triangulation* is an object-level, mathematically natural extremality statement and a certificate stronger than a general homotopy-dimension bound. The ternary Cartesian three-cube is a canonical symmetric graph; its 5-dimensional open-neighborhood complex has nontrivial fundamental group and large second homology. The construction achieves all homological lower bounds on critical cells simultaneously (1,3,56), providing a minimal-cell model and reproducible test instance for combinatorial topology of graph Hom-complexes. This precise optimum is not a renaming of the known group calculation, and no family-wide or canonical attaching-map claim is made.
